subject: english
question:
**Change the following from active to passive:**

We shall have dispatched the invitations before Friday evening.

options.text: The invitations shall have dispatched before Friday evening.
The invitations shall have had been dispatched before Friday evening.
The invitations shall have be dispatched before Friday evening.
The invitations shall have been dispatched before Friday evening.

solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. The invitations shall have been dispatched before Friday evening.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When changing a sentence from active to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the given sentence, **"We shall have dispatched the invitations before Friday evening,"** the object is "the invitations."
 
• The verb in the active voice is "shall have dispatched." In the passive voice, this becomes "shall have been dispatched."
 
• The passive structure for future perfect tense is **Subject + shall/will + have + been + past participle.**

Correct sentence: *The invitations shall have been dispatched before Friday evening.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active to Passive Transformation:**

 
 
• Identify the subject, verb, and object in the active sentence.
 
• Swap the subject with the object, making the object the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• Adjust the verb according to the tense, adding "been" for perfect tenses.
 
 
 
• **Examples:**

 
 
• **Active:** She has finished the project. **Passive:** The project has been finished by her.
 
• **Active:** They will clean the house tomorrow. **Passive:** The house will be cleaned by them tomorrow.
